## Claims
- [source-backed] The inspected paper states that for \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the ideal \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by each of
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
  \]
  [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]
- [source-backed] In the inclusion special case \(t=r\) or \(t=s\), the paper compares its second family with the generators of Gasharov–Reiner (GR02); for \(t=s\), it has \(i=b=1\), \(j=r-s+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-1,s-1)\), and obtains the first \(\min(n-r,s)\) GR02 generators. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 893-933]
- [source-backed] The omitted semantic remark is: “the techniques utilized in [GR02] seem very particular to the case where \(X_w\) is defined by inclusions. We do not know how to use them for some alternate approach to the case of general \(X_w\) considered in this paper.” [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 934-937]
- [source-backed] GR02 is repeatedly referenced: as prior \(n^2\)-generator work for Schubert varieties defined by inclusions (including smooth ones), in the essential-set discussion, in the comparison above, and in the final open question; its bibliography entry is V. Gasharov and V. Reiner, *Cohomology of smooth Schubert varieties in partial flag manifolds*, JLMS 66 (2002), 550–562. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 67-106; 722-729; 900-937; 1143-1160; 1232-1235]
- [source-backed] The paper formally conjectures minimality of both displayed \(J_v\)-families and records only a finite computer verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]

## Strategy
Status: the requested targeted extraction is established from the supplied full text. The current \(J_v\), \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and the two proposed families coincide with the theorem’s objects. GR02 supplies inclusion-case prior work, not a general-\(X_w\) method; the source expressly says this limitation.

## Gaps
The bounded search supplied one full-text candidate only. No separately inspected source here establishes an alternative GR02-based proof for general \(X_w\), nor a theorem beyond the finite range \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\).
